reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a compact topological space with a σ-algebra containing all open sets. Let μ:ℝ→ProbabilityMeasure(E) be weakly continuous, let g:E→ℝ be arbitrary, and let A:ℝ×E→ℝ be jointly continuous. Fix s∈ℝ. Set F(u)=∫_E g(x)dμ_u(x) and B(v)=∫_E A(v,x)dμ_v(x). Suppose that for every u in some ordinary neighborhood of s, F(u)−F(s)=∫_s^u B(v)dv. Then F has the ordinary two-sided derivative F′(s)=B(s).
objects: Compact topological measurable E, a weakly continuous probability-measure curve, observable g, jointly continuous scalar A, point s, and real functions F and B.
domains: The measure curve, F and B have real time. Joint continuity uses ℝ×E with its product topology. The state integrals use the underlying measure of μ at the displayed time.
quantifiers: All displayed structures and data are arbitrary subject to the premises. At the selected s, the balance holds eventually in nhds(s), i.e. throughout some neighborhood of s.
assumptions: Compactness, measurable opens, weak continuity of μ, joint continuity of A and the stated local balance. The displayed proposition imposes no separate measurability, continuity or integrability on g.
conclusion: HasDerivAt of u↦∫_E g dμ_u at s with value ∫_E A(s,x)dμ_s(x).
scopes: The neighborhood covers both sides of s and HasDerivAt is the ordinary unrestricted derivative. The interval integral is oriented: it uses the usual order when the lower endpoint is at most the upper endpoint, changes sign on reversing endpoints, and vanishes when the endpoints coincide. The state integrals are Lean's totalized Bochner integrals, including the integral defining F for arbitrary g.
constant_dependencies: The derivative is the drift average at the same time s with coefficient one.
